images.title: Move one strip: a² − b² becomes a rectangle
images.purpose: Shows that cutting b² from a square of side a and moving one strip makes an (a + b) by (a − b) rectangle.
images.composition: A before and after comparison: on the left the cut square, on the right the rearranged rectangle, with one grey arrow between them. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: Left panel: a square of side a with the b by b top right corner removed and drawn only as a dashed grey (#6B7280) outline. The remaining L shape is in two pieces: a teal (#0072B2) rectangle a wide and a − b tall along the bottom, and an amber (#E69F00) rectangle a − b wide and b tall at the top left. Labels: 'a' under the bottom edge, 'b' beside the dashed corner, 'a² − b²' under the panel. A grey arrow points right. Right panel: the teal rectangle with the amber rectangle turned on its side and attached to its right end, making one rectangle a + b wide and a − b tall. Labels: 'a + b' under the bottom edge, 'a − b' beside the right edge, '(a + b)(a − b)' under the panel. Exactly 2 panels, 1 teal piece and 1 amber piece in each.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The same area is a² − b² and (a + b)(a − b).
images.description: Shows that cutting b² from a square of side a and moving one strip makes an (a + b) by (a − b) rectangle.

image_decisions.why: The cut and slide argument is a picture proof; showing both states makes the identity visible.
